subject: Adaptive repricing framework for unbundled SKUs, distributor COS & velocity credits
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@cloudnine.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@cloudnine.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Repricing ask: unbundling SKUs, distributor cost-of-sale, and velocity credits

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency/cost profile. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so their legal/finance folks can start a private-offer review. High level: CloudNine wants to unbundle a current marketplace bundle into three discrete SKUs (ingest, embeddings, and query), with a staged discount schedule and distributor cost-of-sale (COS) credit that flows to our reseller.

Specific questions we need answered to build our internal MAAP:
- Can Redwood provide a per-SKU list price + a three-step discount waterfall (month 1, month 3, month 6) tied to committed usage bands?
- We need distributor COS details: percentage pass-through to our reseller (they require at least visibility to the margin waterfall and invoice routing).
- Is there a velocity credit mechanism (retroactive) available if CloudNine exceeds higher-tier commit in months 4–6?
- Any constraints for offering the unbundled SKUs on AWS Marketplace private offer (seller/partner pass-through or invoice routing requirements)?

Attached is our current SKU mapping and a draft purchase requirement sheet. Can you loop in pricing/ops folks and get a short-run math simulation (per-month cost to CloudNine + reseller net) for a couple of scenarios?

Target timeline: procurement would like a working draft by Tue, Sep 29 so internal approvals can start.

Appreciate it —
Alex Taylor
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudNine

Attachment stubs: CloudNine_Marketplace_SKU_List.xlsx (spreadsheet), DN-49827-requirements.docx (referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@cloudnine.com>, procure@cloudnine.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Repricing ask: unbundling SKUs, distributor cost-of-sale, and velocity credits

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben (pricing ops) and Irene (channel/marketplace). We can model the scenarios you outlined. Quick notes up-front:

- We can publish per-SKU list prices and create private-offer SKUs that map 1:1 to the unbundled components.
- Discount waterfall is straightforward for committed tiers; retroactive velocity credit is supported but it impacts how we calculate rebate liabilities and payout timing to the distributor.
- Distributor COS pass-through: we typically support a revenue waterfall where reseller receives a defined percentage of net revenue on invoice reconciliation (we'll show both gross-to-net and netback views).
- AWS/GCP/Azure private-offer constraints vary (invoice routing + partner pass-through differ). We'll call that out per-provider.

Ben/Irene — can you run two model permutations:
  1) Conservative: month 1 trial (0–20% commit), month 3 mid (20–60%), month 6 target (>=60%) with COS = 12% pass-through and no retroactive velocity credit.
  2) Aggressive: same tiers but COS = 18% and include a retroactive velocity credit that returns 30% of incremental overage margin to reseller at quarter close.

Deliverable: per-month P&L to CloudNine, reseller netback waterfall, and a short note on marketplace provider constraints for private offers. I'll coordinate with legal on invoice language if/when we get to term-sheet.

I'll aim to have the first draft by Mon Sep 28 EOD.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Partners & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: DN-49827-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal template)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@cloudnine.com>, procure@cloudnine.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Repricing ask: unbundling SKUs, distributor cost-of-sale, and velocity credits

Mina/Irene/Alex — attached is a quick simulation (paste below) for the two scenarios Alex requested. Notes inline.

Scenario inputs (monthly):
- Baseline list prices: ingest $0.006/token, embed 0.0009/vector, query $0.012/query-unit
- Committed bands: Tier A 0–50k units, Tier B 50–250k, Tier C 250k+

Conservative (COS 12%, no velocity):
- Month 1 (trial): CloudNine pays $8,400 (net) / Reseller netback 88% of revenue -> $7,392; Redwood retains 12% COS holdback for partner payout processing
- Month 3: increased usage moves them to Tier B; discount applied 18% off list; reseller netback approx $6,050 after waterfall
- Month 6: at Tier C discount 30% off list; reseller netback calc shown in attached worksheet (see CloudNine_Marketplace_SKU_List.xlsx)

Aggressive (COS 18% + retroactive velocity credit 30% of incremental margin):
- Retro credit mechanics: at quarter close we compute incremental revenue over baseline and pay the reseller 30% of incremental gross margin (after COS). This requires a quarterly reconciliation window (30–45 days) and a DS to the private-offer doc referencing the payout schedule.
- Example: if month 5 shows a spike that lifts them into Tier C, the quarter close calculation returns a one-time credit to the reseller. This reduces Redwood's retained margin so we show both post-credit and pre-credit views.

Marketplace constraints (quick):
- AWS private offers: pass-through is supported but needs seller-managed invoice routing + partner acceptance. Invoice language must reference reseller ID.
- GCP Marketplace: supports commitment-based SKUs but partner pass-through often needs reseller to be an authorized SaaS reseller; additional attestation required.
- Azure: supports multi-SKU offers but invoice splitting options are more limited; could require a downstream rebate workflow.

Action items:
- Mina: confirm whether Redwood will accept a 45-day reconciliation window for retro credits and whether finance signs off on the payout cadence.
- Irene: please draft suggested invoice language for AWS private offer and a fallback clause for Azure.
- Alex: procurement to confirm whether reseller requires immediate invoice routing or a periodic rebate.

Ben Carter
Pricing & Deal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: quick-sim-snapshot pasted into message and full workbook attached.

Thanks — this is super helpful. Procurement confirms they prefer the aggressive plan if Redwood can commit to the 45-day reconciliation and the retro credit payment cadence. A couple follow-ups:

- Can Redwood commit to the quarterly reconciliation mechanics in writing (we can add to the SOW)?
- For AWS private offer, reseller insists on invoice routing on Day 1. Is that feasible or would that force an alternate invoice/rebate flow?
- Please include an example clause for the distributor COS in the draft SOW so our legal team can review.

If you can get a redlineable SOW and the simulation workbook by Tue Sep 29 EOD we'll start internal approvals. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex Taylor
